sara.r: FYI apiserver 503s + etcd leader flips in southamerica-1 starting ~02:04 UTC, cluster reconciles exploding and a surge of GPU attach Pending. looks like controlplane connectivity degrade in one AZ.
ben: saw the GPU attach alerting. scheduler logs show repeated NodeStatus update timeouts and attach retries backoff. pods pile up in Pending -> GPU capacity appears saturated.
kai: pulling tcpdump from a controlplane proxy host — tons of SYN retrans and connection resets to apiserver. ephemeral ports on nat-1 at zero. conntrack counters are not high, so not classic conntrack overflow.
aj: any etcd evidence of corruption or fsync?
sara.r: etcd leader shows intermittent slow syncs + WAL fsync latencies during spikes: ```2026-04-02T02:05:11Z etcdserver: WAL fsync took 462.19ms; backend commit took 512ms``` then leader stepdown a few cycles later. at the same time on proxies: ```time=\"2026-04-02T02:06:03Z\" level=error msg=\"proxy write failed\" err=\"write tcp 10.4.8.6:6443->10.9.1.12:49451: write: connection reset by peer\"```
ben: so two visible symptoms: 1) controlplane TCP churn through NAT causing apiserver proxy exhaustion, 2) etcd WAL tail latency amplified by request bursts -> leader flips. both amplify controller-manager reconcile backlog.
kai: quick mitigation applied: updated route table for the affected AZ to prefer the private control-plane peering (reduces egress via NAT by ~95%). switched apiserver proxies to use the peering IPs. immediate effect: tail error rate down.
aj: cost impact? private peering has an interconnect fee but avoids NAT egress and retries. ben: we estimated short-term bill delta < $200/hr vs ongoing customer impact and GPU attach costs. infra signed off for temporary peering route.
sara.r: other hotfixes: lowered proxy keepalive to 10s, increased proxy FD limit, bumped apiserver --max-mutating-requests-inflight a bit to ease pressure. increased ip_local_port_range on NATs from 32768-60999 -> 20000-65000, and disabled net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse on NAT hosts (set 0). posted sysctl diff in ticket.
kai: also throttled kubelet attach retries from 6s->20s to reduce immediate retry storms. helped steady the reconcile queue.
ben: while peering was switching, we observed etcd leader election traces that looked like: "leader lost quorum, start campaign" aligning with network blips. plan: move etcd client traffic off NAT path entirely and ensure peers talk over private network.
aj: long term proposals: 1) make controlplane peering the primary path for control-plane traffic in all regions with GPUs, 2) add a small pool of dedicated controlplane NATs with enlarged ephemeral ranges on standby, 3) build a synthetic that simulates 10k keepalive churn to detect smear during deploys, 4) revisit kernel patch that enabled aggressive TIME_WAIT reuse in the image build.
sara.r: created incident INC-2026-400 and linked runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/controlplane-connectivity. tagging infra + oncall for 48h watch.
ops-bot: Alert: incident INC-2026-400 opened by sara.r (sev: high)
ben: scoreboard after the peering switch and quick tunables: apiserver 5xx trend down from ~8/min -> ~0.9/min, controller-manager queue from ~11k -> 600, GPU attach Pending in that AZ down 78%.
kai: follow-ups assigned: I will own kernel rollback testing in non-prod and the nat ephemeral range audit. ben will coordinate peering deployment and cost runbook. sara.r will own postmortem.
aj: good. also add a short-term billing note for customers routed through peering so finance can annotate invoices if needed.
sara.r: noted. moving full discussion to the incident channel and creating postmortem draft after 24h stable. closing thread here. :white_check_mark:
